docs.title: What is Java?
docs.text:
Java is a high-level, object-oriented, platform-independent programming language developed by Sun Microsystems (now owned by Oracle).

It is designed to be: - Simple - Secure - Robust - Portable

Java follows the principle: "Write Once, Run Anywhere (WORA)"

docs.title: Why Learn Java?
docs.text:
Java is one of the most in-demand programming languages.

It is widely used in: - Web applications - Android mobile apps - Enterprise systems - Automation testing (Selenium, TestNG)

✔ Beginner-friendly ✔ Huge community support ✔ Used in real-world projects

docs.title: Platform Independent
docs.text: Java code can run on any system that has JVM installed.

docs.title: Object-Oriented
docs.text: Everything in Java is based on objects and classes.

docs.title: Secure
docs.text: Java does not use pointers and has built-in security features.

docs.title: Robust
docs.text: Strong memory management and exception handling.

docs.title: Multithreaded
docs.text: Java supports running multiple tasks at the same time.

docs.title: Java Architecture (VERY IMPORTANT)
docs.text: Java works using three main components:

docs.title: 1. JVM (Java Virtual Machine)
docs.text:
JVM is the engine that runs Java programs.

Responsibilities: - Executes bytecode - Converts bytecode into machine code - Manages memory - Handles garbage collection

✔ Platform dependent ✔ Core of Java runtime

docs.title: 2. JRE (Java Runtime Environment)
docs.text:
JRE provides the environment to run Java programs.

It includes: - JVM - Libraries - Runtime files

✔ Used only for running Java programs

docs.title: 3. JDK (Java Development Kit)
docs.text:
JDK is used for developing Java applications.

It includes: - JRE - Compiler (javac) - Tools (debugger, etc.)

✔ Used for writing + compiling + running

docs.title: Relationship
docs.text:
JDK = JRE + Development Tools
JRE = JVM + Libraries

docs.title: Arithmetic Rules
docs.text:
• [ ] Integer division truncates - always cast to double for decimals
  • [ ] Modulo sign follows dividend: -5 % 3 = -2, 5 % -3 = 2

docs.title: Increment/Decrement Rules

• [ ] Pre (++a): Change first, then use (for immediate updates)
  • [ ] Post (a++): Use first, then change (for current value preservation)
  • [ ] Never chain multiple increments in one expression
  • [ ] In loops, post-increment (i++) is standard convention

            // Element not found - increase wait
            retryCount += 1;
            System.out.println("Retry #" + retryCount);

            // Exponential backoff: double the wait
            baseWait *= 2;

            // Cap at maximum
            if (baseWait > maxWait) {
                baseWait = maxWait;
                System.out.println("Reached max wait: " + baseWait + "s");
            } else {
                System.out.println("Increased wait to: " + baseWait + "s");
            }

            // Check if max retries reached
            if (retryCount >= 5) {
                System.out.println("Max retries reached. Failing test.");
                break;
            }
        }

        System.out.println("\n=== SUMMARY ===");
        System.out.println("Total retries this session: " + retryCount);

        scanner.close();
    }
}

import java.util.Scanner;

public class SeleniumWaitBuilder {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Scanner scanner = new Scanner(System.in);

        System.out.println("=== Selenium Smart Wait Builder ===");

        // Simulating element states
        System.out.print("Element exists (true/false): ");
        boolean exists = scanner.nextBoolean();

        System.out.print("Element is visible (true/false): ");
        boolean visible = scanner.nextBoolean();

        System.out.print("Element is enabled (true/false): ");
        boolean enabled = scanner.nextBoolean();

        System.out.print("Element text is not empty (true/false): ");
        boolean hasText = scanner.nextBoolean();

        System.out.print("Loading spinner present (true/false): ");
        boolean loading = scanner.nextBoolean();

        System.out.print("Error message displayed (true/false): ");
        boolean errorDisplayed = scanner.nextBoolean();

        // Standard clickable condition
        boolean isClickable = exists && visible && enabled && !loading;

        // Safe to interact (no errors, ready state)
        boolean safeToInteract = isClickable && !errorDisplayed;

        // Ready for assertion (text loaded, stable)
        boolean readyForCheck = exists && visible && hasText && !loading;

        // Wait should continue (not ready yet)
        boolean shouldKeepWaiting = !safeToInteract && !errorDisplayed;

        // Fail fast condition (error state)
        boolean shouldFail = errorDisplayed || (exists && !visible && !loading);

        System.out.println("\n=== Wait Logic ===");
        System.out.println("Element clickable: " + isClickable);
        System.out.println("Safe to interact: " + safeToInteract);
        System.out.println("Ready for assertion: " + readyForCheck);
        System.out.println("⏳ Continue waiting: " + shouldKeepWaiting);
        System.out.println("❌ Fail test: " + shouldFail);

        // Complex wait strategy
        System.out.println("\n=== Recommended Action ===");
        if (safeToInteract) {
            System.out.println("✅ PROCEED: Click/interact with element");
        } else if (shouldFail) {
            System.out.println("❌ ABORT: Error state detected");
        } else if (!exists) {
            System.out.println("⏳ WAIT: Element not in DOM yet");
        } else if (loading) {
            System.out.println("⏳ WAIT: Page still loading");
        } else if (!visible) {
            System.out.println("⏳ WAIT: Element not visible (scrolling/animation?)");
        } else if (!enabled) {
            System.out.println("⏳ WAIT: Element disabled");
        }

        // Timeout calculation
        int baseTimeout = 10;
        int extendedTimeout = (loading || !exists) ? baseTimeout * 2 : baseTimeout;
        System.out.println("Suggested timeout: " + extendedTimeout + " seconds");

        scanner.close();
    }
}

docs.title: ✅ Logical Rules
docs.text:
• [ ] && (AND): Both must be true
  • [ ] \|\| (OR): At least one must be true
  • [ ] ! (NOT): Reverses boolean
  • [ ] Short-circuit: Evaluation stops when result is known
  • [ ] Precedence: ! > && > \|\| (use parentheses!)

docs.title: ✅ Best Practices
docs.text:
• [ ] Put cheaper/lighter checks first for short-circuit benefit
  • [ ] Use parentheses to make complex logic readable
  • [ ] Decompose complex conditions into named booleans
  • [ ] Use ! sparingly - positive conditions are easier to read
  • [ ] For null checks, put null check BEFORE method call: if (obj != null && obj.isValid())
